short: Multi-scale TCN back end (M06) and variable-length training (M03) are standard: TCN beats BGRU by 0.7 points in one run; robustness comes from the cropping; 85.3% LRW trails 93.2% today.
position: The paper [@martinez2020tcn] changes the temporal back end (M06), a multi-scale dilated TCN in place of a BGRU, and the training recipe (M03), single-stage cosine training with variable-length temporal cropping. Both are standard. Temporal convolution on LRW predates it as a shallow warm-up stage [@stafylakis2017resnetlstm; @stafylakis2018pushing]; the multi-scale form has no prior pattern hit, but its gain over the BGRU is 0.7 points against the fixed-length BGRU in one run on one dataset (Table 2), and a [later] matched-recipe test gives 90.0% vs 89.7% [@ma2022trainingstrategies]. Frame-drop robustness comes from the cropping: TCN and BGRU trained the same way keep about the same share of accuracy with five frames removed. LRW-1000 has no own BGRU baseline, no run counts are reported, and the noise experiment names no corpus. Today 85.3% on LRW trails 93.2% without word boundaries [@ahn2024syncvsr].
